findings.summary: Cheliped field report (plugin v1.36.0): while ANY session held a TEST-LOCK, every session's writes to OUT-OF-ROOT paths (memory ~/.claude/projects, plan-mode ~/.claude/plans, scratchpad) were BLOCKED — edit_findings converted policy_decision's 'target escapes repository root' ContractError into a block, a cross-session denial-of-service that also broke plan-mode (whose only permitted write is the out-of-root plan file). An out-of-root target is out of the lock's jurisdiction, not a policy violation.
findings.disposition: edit_findings now pre-checks _inside(root, target) (the same helper the Bash leg uses for cwd) and returns no findings for out-of-root targets. The regression lives in the BLESSED suite (test_tdd_lock.py::test_out_of_root_jurisdiction), red-first proven in a REAL git repo — the bug fires only where resolve_repository succeeds and policy_decision is reached, so a non-git scratch fixture would be vacuous; reverting reproduces the exact reported 'escapes repository root' error. Two-directional: in-root locked test still BLOCKS, out-of-root write ALLOWS.

findings.summary: Cheliped secondary observation: an UNDECIDABLE write target (open(var,'w'), a heredoc writer) while a lock is active fails closed BY DESIGN, but _seg_writes returned True for it against the FIRST needle checked, so the block message named a locked test the write may not even touch — misdirecting the operator.
findings.disposition: Split _seg_writes (needle-specific) from _has_undecidable_write; bash_findings gives the undecidable case an honest 'target the guard cannot resolve' message while keeping the fail-closed behavior. Pinned by test_tdd_lock (undecidable write blocks with the honest message, not the test name).

findings.summary: Cheliped near-miss: a security control shipped with 9 green tests over an INERT gate — it authorized off an ambient contextvar a new caller never published, and the tests SEEDED that contextvar by hand instead of driving the production entry that sets it. Self-consistency; mutation blind (mutants in the guard, test seeds its input).
findings.disposition: SKILL §1 new rule ('drive a guard through the entry that populates its input — never seed the input by hand', with the grep-able tell), §4 mutation-blindness note, and hunt #6 on the security + test-quality adversaries (registered as gate-surface change L-20260815-01, burial-check prediction). The planted calibration anchor per §13 is dated debt (calibration-loop, exp 2026-11-15) — doctrine without a planted anchor is unproven, recorded as a loan not a hope.

findings.summary: The holdout is opt-in, so a run that never happens is a date that never advances — it could go dark silently (David: 'don't let it go dark without a date or a schedule').
findings.disposition: holdout_staleness (via history_format.latest_form_date) surfaces 'Last run: N days ago (STALE > 30d)' in the --summary output AND as a HOLDOUT-STALE WARNING on EVERY calibration run — the 'date' that keeps it from going dark, no budget or cron. An actual autonomous scheduler (launchd) is deferred pending David's cadence decision (Keychain / autonomous-spend / silent-failure gotchas). Tested fresh/stale/none/summary-surfaces.
